fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker! Forty years with no bread, no wine and no strong drink, and the reason is right there: “…so that you might know that I am the LORD your God.” Forty years! I can't make it forty minutes without a cookie. The LORD gives them one reason, and it's about knowing who He is.

They're actually in, friend. Moses names “…the foreigners in your camps who cut your wood and draw your water…” among those standing before the LORD. They're listed so that they may enter into the covenant (Deuteronomy 29:11 and 12). They're named right there in the verse.

Right, they are not left out. Moses lists them among those standing before the LORD: “…the foreigners in your camps who cut your wood and draw your water…” The list is there so that they may enter into the covenant (Deuteronomy 29:12). They're named right in the verse.

Yes. Moses says, “You saw the abominations and idols among them made of wood and stone, of silver and gold.” They'd passed through those nations on the way here, and they'd seen it for themselves. Wood, stone, silver and gold, that's the whole list.

Poisonous and bitter, that's it. Moses says the root “…bears such poisonous and bitter fruit…” Just before that, he warns about hearts turning away from the LORD. Nothing sweet on that branch, baker. It's a serious warning, so I'll leave it right there.

That's the opposite of what Moses says. The root “…bears such poisonous and bitter fruit…” Sweet and plentiful is not on the branch. He gives this warning right after warning about hearts turning away from the LORD (Deuteronomy 29:18), so it's a serious one.

Fair guess, but Moses doesn't say small or hidden. He says the root “…bears such poisonous and bitter fruit…” Those are his exact words for it. It comes right after his warning about hearts turning away from the LORD (Deuteronomy 29:18).

That's what Moses says: the LORD “…will blot out his name from under heaven” It's a heavy thing to read, friend, and I think it hurts a little. Moses says it in the middle of a warning about turning away from the LORD (Deuteronomy 29:18 to 20).
